Local Tastes
Testi Kebabı
Lamb or beef slow-cooked with vegetables inside a sealed clay pot, then cracked open tableside — a central Anatolian specialty tied to Cappadocia's pottery towns.
Smoky Kebap & Steak Restaurant · TUMA Restaurant · Göreme Han Restaurant
Cappadocian Wine
Wine grown in volcanic soil at high altitude from native grapes like Emir, Narince, and Kalecik Karası — a winemaking tradition in the region dating back millennia.
Turasan Winery · Ürgüp
Food Delivery
Yemeksepeti
Foreign number: not accepted — Yemeksepeti's own sign-up help page states a membership cannot be created with a non-Turkish mobile number.
Turkey's largest delivery platform reaches restaurants in Göreme itself, though coverage in Cappadocia's small villages is thinner than in Istanbul or Ankara — expect fewer listed restaurants and longer delivery windows than a big city.
yemeksepeti.com
Getting Around
No ride-hailing app operates in Göreme — Uber does not run in Turkey, and BiTaksi and InDrive have no meaningful driver coverage in Cappadocia. Every hotel front desk calls a taxi directly, or visitors flag one at the taxi rank by the Göreme bus station; day tours and hotel transfers otherwise cover most trips.

Worth Knowing

One volcano explains the caves, the wine, and the balloons

Every fairy chimney, cave church, and underground city in this guide is carved from the same material: soft volcanic tuff laid down by eruptions from Erciyes and Hasan Dağ millions of years ago, then sculpted by wind and rain into the cones and valleys the region is known for. That same soft rock is why people could dig into it by hand — early Christian communities carved chapels and whole refuge cities into it starting in the Byzantine era, and the tradition never really stopped; the cave hotel rooms booked for this trip are dug the same way, just with plumbing.

Cappadocia is one of the few places on Earth where hot air ballooning runs on most mornings of the year, and that is also a product of the landscape: the valleys sit in a natural bowl that traps still air at dawn before the day's wind picks up, giving pilots a predictable calm window that flatter terrain elsewhere cannot offer. It is the same volcanic soil, incidentally, that gives the region's wine its character — grapes grown in it are said to carry a faint mineral note the locals call tasting like the mountain.
